problem: The first v3 retrain completed only 150 gradient updates in 3 hours and the policy degraded (grasp 0.20 -> 0.00) with critic_loss still diverging (0.15 -> 8.39). The obvious reading -- 'the fixes made it worse' -- is wrong; the run never had enough optimiser steps to fit a freshly initialised critic.

measurement.where_the_time_goes: Each chunk decision costs 30 actions x 2 sim substeps = 60 simulator steps plus a VLM forward. At 479 ms per env step the run collected only 376 chunk decisions in 3 hours, which at UTD 0.5 yields ~188 updates.
measurement.the_original_run_for_comparison: The 415k RLPD checkpoint reached 2983 updates by running ~415k env steps (roughly 50 hours) at the SAME UTD 0.5 -- not by being more efficient per step.

measured_optimiser_cost.note: VLM features are cached in the replay buffer, so an update does not re-run the VLM.

conclusion: The bottleneck is simulation and VLM rollout throughput, not the optimiser. Raising the update-to-data ratio buys gradient updates at ~0.1% wall-clock overhead. UTD 8 reaches the original run's 2983 updates within a single 3-hour budget.
caveat: High UTD on a small replay buffer risks overfitting the critic to limited data -- the standard reason UTD is kept low. Two things mitigate it here: RLPD fills half of every batch from the 22-episode demonstration buffer, and the DCT basis cut the critic's input from 900 to 180 dimensions, raising transitions-per-input-dimension from 8.2 to 41. The run must still be watched for critic divergence, which is why critic_loss is a reported readout.

CORRECTION_after_run_2.what_was_projected: This contract projected that raising UTD to 8 would cost ~13 s over a 3-hour run (0.12% overhead) and yield ~3000 gradient updates, based on a measured critic update of 4.66 ms.
CORRECTION_after_run_2.why_the_projection_was_wrong: The 4.66 ms timing measured ONLY the critic MLP. It excluded demo_batch, where a cache MISS runs two vlm_encode calls. A direct measurement puts vlm_encode at 107.5 ms, so a miss costs 215 ms. RLPD draws BATCH*DEMO_FRAC = 4 demo transitions per update, so at UTD 8 the loop can pay up to 8 x 4 x 2 = 64 encodes per environment decision while the cache fills. Benchmarking a component and presenting it as the system cost is the error.
CORRECTION_after_run_2.second_cost_found: The step-0 evaluations (init and init_stochastic) run 2 x N_EVAL_PERIODIC x EP_CHUNKS = 1150 chunk rollouts BEFORE any gradient step. For both runs that is the single largest block of work, and it duplicates a v3 baseline already scored under the same predicate.

fixes.PREWARM_DEMO_CACHE: Encode every demonstration transition once before training: 489 transitions x 2 encodes x 107.5 ms = ~105 s, one time. After that demo_batch is a dict lookup and UTD scales on MLP cost as originally intended.
fixes.RUN_INIT_EVAL: Allows skipping the step-0 evaluations when the warm-start checkpoint has already been scored under the same predicate, freeing ~1150 chunk rollouts.

CORRECTION_after_run_2.method_note: Two throughput projections in this project have now been wrong in the same way -- extrapolating from a measured piece rather than the measured whole. Any future throughput claim should be validated by a short end-to-end run before a long one is launched.

end_to_end_validation_2026_08_31.method: Following the method note added after run 2 -- validate a throughput claim with a short END-TO-END run before launching a long one -- a 20-minute probe was run with the fixes on (PREWARM_DEMO_CACHE=1, RUN_INIT_EVAL=0, UTD=8) and the real loop timed.

with_fixes_utd_8.note: projection now rests on an end-to-end measurement of the real loop, not on a component timing

end_to_end_validation_2026_08_31.improvement: 33x faster per gradient update than run 1, 39x faster than run 2.
end_to_end_validation_2026_08_31.interpretation: The two costs identified were the whole story: demonstration VLM cache misses inside the update loop, and 1150 step-0 evaluation rollouts before any training. With both removed, a 3-hour budget supports roughly 4900 gradient updates -- more than the 2983 the original 415k checkpoint accumulated over ~50 hours.
end_to_end_validation_2026_08_31.critic_health_during_the_probe: critic_loss 1.04 -> 0.053 -> 0.052 over the first 75 updates: settling, not diverging. Contrast run 1, which ended at 8.39 and rising.

revision_at_600s.why: The 300 s sample gave 2.19 s/update; the 600 s sample gives a MARGINAL rate of 6.0 s/update (cumulative 3.72). Projecting from the earlier figure would have repeated the exact error this contract already documents twice.
revision_at_600s.finding: The SIMULATOR is the dominant fixed cost at ~830 ms per step, independent of UTD. The demo cache prewarm and skipped init evals removed the two costs that scaled WITH UTD, which is why UTD 8 is now affordable at all -- but they cannot make collection itself faster.

corrected_projection.supersedes: the 4859 figure, which extrapolated the pre-amortisation rate

revision_at_600s.still_a_large_improvement: Run 1 achieved 150 updates and run 2 achieved 125 in the same budget, so 1800-2900 is a 12-19x improvement and comparable to the 2983 updates the original 415k checkpoint accumulated over ~50 hours.
revision_at_600s.method_note: Third time this project has had to correct a throughput projection. The rule now applied: quote the MARGINAL rate from a steady-state window, never a cumulative rate that still contains one-time costs.

clean_probe_all_three_fixes.third_cost_found: A step-0 PERIODIC evaluation also fired regardless of EVAL_EVERY, because next_eval started at 0. That is 25 conditions x 23 chunks = 575 rollouts. The first probe spent its ENTIRE 20-minute budget inside it -- updates frozen at 125 for 15 minutes -- which is what identified it. The code comment had flagged this as removable once the original SAC/RLPD arms finished; they had.

progression_of_the_three_projections.1st_component_timing: 4.66 ms critic MLP -> predicted 3000 updates. WRONG: excluded VLM encodes.
progression_of_the_three_projections.2nd_cumulative_rate: 2.19 s/update at 300 s -> predicted 4859. WRONG: still contained the amortised prewarm.
progression_of_the_three_projections.3rd_clean_end_to_end: 1.54 s/update over 225 updates with all three fixes -> ~6900 in 3 h.
progression_of_the_three_projections.discipline_adopted: quote a marginal or post-amortisation rate from a steady-state window, measured end to end.

critic_health_during_the_probe.reading: Spiky but MEAN-REVERTING: every spike recovers (2.48 -> 0.38, 4.65 -> 0.46). Run 1 by contrast ended at 8.39 and rising with no recovery. Q_mean climbing 0.19 -> 1.37 is the thing to watch in the full run: with a fresh critic it can be genuine value learning or the onset of overestimation, and 250 updates cannot distinguish them.
